hero.caption: Green fig, cold iris and smoked vetiver. *Scroll to wear it*: each screen is time on your skin.

end.caption: Nine hours later the ambrette is still there. *Three sprays* carry you from breakfast to dinner.

tiers.name: Top notes
tiers.caption: First 15 minutes: *bright and green*. Bergamot and fig leaf are the lightest molecules, so they leave first.

tiers.name: Heart notes
tiers.caption: From 15 minutes to 3 hours the iris comes through: *cool, powdery, a little smoky*.

tiers.name: Base notes
tiers.caption: After 3 hours: *vetiver, cedar and musk*, close to your skin until evening.

notes.name: Bergamot
notes.smell: The first scratch of an orange peel, but sharper and more floral. Bright for ten minutes, then gone.
notes.material: Cold-pressed peel oil, Calabria. Bergaptene removed so it's safe in sunlight.

notes.name: Fig leaf
notes.smell: Snapping a fig leaf off the branch in July: green, milky sap and a bitter edge.
notes.material: Fig leaf absolute blended with stemone, a green-fig molecule.

notes.name: Pink pepper
notes.smell: A dry, rosy fizz at the back of the nose. No heat at all; it's a berry, not a pepper.
notes.material: CO₂ extract of Schinus molle berries, Réunion.

notes.name: Orris butter
notes.smell: Cool and powdery, close to an old lipstick, with a raw-carrot earthiness underneath.
notes.material: Iris rhizomes dried for three years, then steam-distilled. Costs more per kilo than silver.

notes.name: Fig milk
notes.smell: The sap inside a ripe fig: soft, a little coconut, like warm milk on the stove.
notes.material: Lactones and a touch of coconut aldehyde. No real fig gives up its smell, so it's built.

notes.name: Black tea
notes.smell: Smoked lapsang leaves. Dry and leathery, like a teapot left out overnight.
notes.material: Black tea absolute with a trace of birch tar for the smoke.

notes.name: Vetiver
notes.smell: Earthy and clean, like soil after a storm, with a grapefruit edge that keeps it from going dark.
notes.material: Haitian vetiver root oil, distilled from 18-month roots.

notes.name: Cedarwood
notes.smell: Pencil shavings and dry sawdust. It gives the drydown its spine.
notes.material: Atlas cedarwood oil from fallen trees, Morocco.

notes.name: Ambrette seed
notes.smell: A plant musk: warm skin, a little pear. It's what stays closest to you at the end of the day.
notes.material: Steam-distilled hibiscus seeds. A plant swap for animal musk.

notesSection.title: What you smell, *and when.*
notesSection.lede: Perfumers stack a scent like a pyramid. The light molecules at the top leave first; the heavy ones at the base stay into the evening. Tap a note to read what it smells like.

wear.title: Spray where *the blood runs warm.*
wear.lede: Pulse points sit where veins run close to the skin. The warmth lifts the scent off you as you move. Tap a point.

pulse.name: Behind the ears
pulse.tip: Warm skin close to your face, so people catch it when you lean in to say hello. The orris shows up best here.

pulse.name: Base of the throat
pulse.tip: The warmest pulse point you can reach. Body heat lifts the heart notes, so this is where you'll smell it yourself through the day.

pulse.name: Inner elbows
pulse.tip: Covered by sleeves, so it lasts longer. You get small bursts of cedar every time you bend your arm.

pulse.name: Wrists
pulse.dose: 1 spray each, then let it dry
pulse.tip: Don't rub your wrists together. The friction heats the skin and burns off the bergamot in a couple of minutes.

pulse.name: On a scarf
pulse.tip: Wool and cotton hold the base notes for days. Skip silk and pale fabrics: the oils can leave a mark.

results.title: The green hour
results.text: You'll like the **first 15 minutes** best, when the fig leaf is sharp and green. Spray again at lunch to bring it back.

results.title: The powder hour
results.text: You'll like it most **after the first hour**, when the orris comes through cool and powdery.

results.title: The smoke hour
results.text: You'll like it most **in the evening**, when the vetiver and black tea smoke are all that's left.
